tagline: The education hub of central Isan — Phra That Na Dun, ancient Khmer ruins, and a lively student scene
introHtml: Maha Sarakham is an education town in the heart of Isan. Two big universities fill the place with students, cafes, and budget-friendly restaurants. Around town you'll find Phra That Na Dun, considered the Buddhist center of the northeast, scattered Khmer-era ruins across several districts, and craft villages where people still do real basketry and weaving. If you want small-town Isan that's easy to get around, where food is cheap and there's history to track down, Maha Sarakham is worth a stop.
bestTime: November–February, cool and comfortable — good for walking the town and tracking down the old Khmer ruins

highlights.name: Phra That Na Dun
highlights.blurb: The Buddhist center of Isan in Na Dun district, where Buddha relics and Dvaravati-era artifacts were found. It's the spiritual heart of Maha Sarakham.

highlights.name: Mahasarakham University
highlights.blurb: This is a student town. The area around the university is packed with dorms, restaurants, and cafes that stay open late.

highlights.name: Ku Santarat and the ancient ruins
highlights.blurb: A Khmer-era stone sanctuary in Na Dun district that once served as an arogayasala, an old hospital — a clear trace of Khmer civilization.

highlights.name: Kaeng Loeng Chan
highlights.blurb: A reservoir near town where locals come to catch the breeze, cycle, and grab a riverside bite in the evening.

highlights.name: Ban Mo pottery village
highlights.blurb: An old pottery village in Mueang district where people still throw clay pots and household ware by hand the traditional way.

highlights.name: Maha Sarakham's museums and antiquities
highlights.blurb: The town holds plenty of Dvaravati- and Khmer-era artifacts. Track down the carved stone boundary markers and terracotta votive tablets dug up around the area.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken eaten with sticky rice — found on every corner, bold and fiery the way real Isan food is.

foodScene.name: Food around the university
foodScene.note: The Tha Khon Yang area and the streets around MSU are full of rice-and-curry stalls, made-to-order shops, and student-priced snacks open till late.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha and jim jum
foodScene.note: DIY grill-and-hotpot joints are all over town — a go-to dinner for students and workers alike.

foodScene.name: Isan sausage and mam
foodScene.note: Tangy fermented sausages grilled and eaten with fresh vegetables and sticky rice — both a snack and a classic local souvenir.

foodScene.name: Cafes and coffee
foodScene.note: Being a student town means lots of cafes around the university and in the center — good for working or reading all day.

foodScene.name: Noodles and bites by Kaeng Loeng Chan
foodScene.note: Restaurants and snack stalls line the reservoir, easy to settle in for a meal in the cool evening breeze.

foodScene.name: Pla ra and local ferments
foodScene.note: Pla ra, jaew bong, and other punchy ferments are staples of the Isan kitchen — pick them up at the town's fresh markets.

foodScene.name: Morning markets and night markets
foodScene.note: The town markets have breakfast bites from sticky rice with grilled pork to khanom jeen, plus grilled snacks to graze on at night.

attractions.name: Phra That Na Dun
attractions.blurb: The Buddhist center of Isan in Na Dun district, where Buddha relics and Dvaravati-era artifacts were found. It's revered across the whole province.

attractions.name: Ku Santarat
attractions.blurb: A Khmer-era stone sanctuary that once served as an arogayasala, a trace of Khmer civilization in Na Dun district where the structure is still clearly visible.

attractions.name: Ku Ban Khwao
attractions.blurb: Another Khmer-era ruin in Mueang district, good for anyone who likes tracking down the old stone sanctuaries of Isan.

attractions.name: Kaeng Loeng Chan
attractions.blurb: A reservoir near town that's a favorite spot for locals to relax, with a cycling path and viewpoints along the water.

attractions.name: Don Chao Pu, Ban Nong Khu
attractions.blurb: A sacred grove that's still home to a troop of monkeys. People like to stop by to feed them and stroll under the trees.

attractions.name: Ban Mo pottery village
attractions.blurb: A pottery village in Mueang district where you can watch locals throw clay pots and household ware by hand the traditional way.

attractions.name: Mahasarakham University
attractions.blurb: A large campus with a lively student quarter around its walls, full of restaurants and cafes.

attractions.name: Wat Maha Chai and Phra Urangkhathat
attractions.blurb: An old temple in the town center that keeps palm-leaf manuscripts and antiquities — a spiritual anchor for the community.
